question.text: Which of the following investments eligible under Section 80C has the SHORTEST lock-in period?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says ELSS has a compulsory 3-year lock-in, which is the shortest among the tax-saving instruments listed. The comparison table on page 421 also shows ELSS at 3 years, PPF at 15 years, and a tax-saving bank FD locked in for its deposit tenure. The Trap: All four options are 80C-eligible, but only ELSS at 3 years is shorter than the 5-year tax-saving FD and far shorter than the 15-year PPF lock-in. Note: Compared with PPF (15 years) and a 5-year tax-saving bank FD, ELSS gives a meaningfully shorter compulsory lock-in.
